items.title: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 for HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. The efficacy and safety of anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801) in this context are unknown.
METHODS: In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point.
RESULTS: A total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; P<0.001). The percentage of patients with an objective response was 87.6% in the anbenitamab group and 73.4% in the THP group. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 204 of 444 patients (45.9%) in the anbenitamab group and in 151 of 439 patients (34.4%) in the THP group. Neutropenia was the most common adverse event of grade 3 or higher in both groups (13.1% in the anbenitamab group and 8.4% in the THP group). Adverse events leading to death occurred in 2 patients in each group.
CONCLUSIONS: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. (Funded by Shanghai JMT-Bio Technology and others; HEALER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05838066.).

items.title: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ganfeborole and BTZ-043 are new drugs that may improve tuberculosis treatment.
METHODS: In this phase 2, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned participants with rifampin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis to receive the standard four-drug combination (isoniazid-rifampin-pyrazinamide-ethambutol; HRZE) for 24 weeks; bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin for 16 weeks; or one of 10 new four-drug combinations for 16 weeks. The new regimens contained ganfeborole, BTZ-043, or both, with combinations of bedaquiline, delamanid, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide, pretomanid, and linezolid. The primary end point was the log10(time to positivity) slope (rate of change from baseline to week 12 in the time to Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a positive sputum culture). The treatment effect was assessed as the Bayesian posterior probability of superiority of each new regimen to HRZE with respect to the primary end point (results were used to select regimens for further evaluation, rather than for characterization of efficacy).
RESULTS: A total of 401 participants underwent randomization; 371 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 400 in the safety population. We identified two promising regimens for further evaluation: ganfeborole-bedaquiline-pretomanid-moxifloxacin (BPMG) and BTZ-043-bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin (BDMT). The log10(time to positivity) slope was 0.129 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.112 to 0.146) with BPMG and 0.142 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.126 to 0.160) with BDMT, as compared with 0.118 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.105 to 0.131) with HRZE, for a relative difference of 9.1% (95% Bayesian credible interval, -8.6 to 29.0) and 20.5% (95% Bayesian credible interval, 2.7 to 41.1), respectively, and a posterior probability of superiority of 0.83 and 0.99. The incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was 38% in the BPMG group (none of the participants discontinued), 28% in the BDMT group (one discontinued because of a drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms), and 24% in the HRZE group (none discontinued). Bedaquiline-moxifloxacin-pyrazinamide-BTZ-043 was discontinued because of hepatotoxic effects.
CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, two four-drug regimens, one with ganfeborole and one with BTZ-043, showed evidence of potential efficacy and a safety profile that did not preclude progression to further evaluation. (Funded by Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking and others; PARADIGM4TB ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06114628.).

items.title: Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in STEMI.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The safety of omitting up-front treatment with aspirin during primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in Japan involving patients with STEMI who were undergoing primary PCI. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio before PCI to receive low-dose prasugrel monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and low-dose prasugrel for 12 months. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction at 12 months, which was assessed for noninferiority with a prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.50 for the 95% confidence interval of the hazard ratio. The major secondary outcome was major bleeding (defined as a bleeding event of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium [BARC] type 3 [nonfatal major bleeding] or 5 [fatal bleeding]) at 12 months, which was assessed for superiority if noninferiority was established for the primary outcome.
RESULTS: A total of 2216 patients were included in the full analysis population; 1109 were assigned to receive monotherapy and 1107 to receive DAPT. At 12 months, death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction had occurred in 124 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 11.0%) in the monotherapy group and in 94 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 8.5%) in the DAPT group (hazard ratio, 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02 to 1.75; P = 0.40 for noninferiority). Major bleeding had occurred in 61 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 5.6%) in the monotherapy group and in 92 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 8.4%) in the DAPT group (hazard ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.91). The percentages of patients with definite or probable stent thrombosis and serious adverse events appeared to be similar in the two groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with STEMI who were undergoing primary PCI, low-dose prasugrel monotherapy initiated before PCI was not noninferior to DAPT for 12 months with respect to a composite of death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction at 12 months. (Funded by Boston Scientific Japan; PREMIUM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05709626.).

items.title: Computed Tomography Screening and Small Cell Lung Cancer Stage Shift and Survival.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) has been shown to identify lung cancers at earlier stages and to significantly reduce lung cancer mortality in prior randomized clinical trials. However, the benefit of LDCT screening for small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive subtype of lung cancer, is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the characteristics and outcomes of SCLC diagnosed after a lung cancer screening examination using a large database of Medicare beneficiaries.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this retrospective cohort study, Medicare data linked to the Surveillance Epidemiology End Results Program's cancer registry data were analyzed. Patients in the US aged 65 to 78 years who were diagnosed with SCLC from 2015 to 2021 were identified for analysis, with follow-up data through 2022. Patients who underwent 1 or more LDCT lung cancer screening examinations during the 12 months preceding their SCLC diagnosis were included in the screened group. All other patients were included in the unscreened group. Data were analyzed from January to August 2026.
EXPOSURE: One or more LDCT lung cancer screenings during the 12 months preceding SCLC diagnosis.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were stage at SCLC diagnosis and overall survival after SCLC diagnosis in the screened and unscreened groups.
RESULTS: A total of 17 099 patients (median [IQR] age, 72.0 [69.0-75.0] years; 8999 [52.6%] female) met study inclusion criteria, of which 949 (5.5%) were included in the screened group and 16 150 (94.5%) were included in the unscreened group. When compared with patients in the unscreened group, patients in the screened group were significantly less likely to be diagnosed with distant disease (419 of 949 [44.2%] vs 11 376 of 16 150 [70.4%]; P < .001). Patients in the screened group also had significantly better overall survival when compared with patients in the unscreened group (3-year overall survival, 28.0% [95% CI, 24.9%-31.2%] vs 10.8% [95% CI, 10.3%-11.3%]; P < .001). Both findings were consistent in propensity score-matched analysis.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries diagnosed with SCLC suggest that receipt of lung cancer screening was associated with a shift toward earlier-stage SCLC at diagnosis and improved overall survival.

items.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days.
RESULTS: A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group).
CONCLUSIONS: In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

items.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.
RESULTS: A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

items.title: Repeated sugar exposure reshapes cue-potentiated motivation without a detectable change in explicit valuation.
items.abstract: The degree to which habitual consumption of rewarding foods shapes responses to environmental food cues remains poorly understood. Preclinical research suggests that sugar exposure alters neural mechanisms that underlie motivated behavior and increases the influence of reward-predictive cues. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT03490734), adults consumed a sucrose-sweetened or a flavor-matched, unsweetened, non-caloric control beverage daily for 3 weeks (n = 160; n = 122 neuroimaging subsample). Repeated sugar exposure increased approach speed toward the beverage cue, which was associated with differences in ventral striatal cue response between groups. This occurred without detectable between-group changes in sugary beverage valuation, body mass, or diet. In exploratory analyses at follow-up, the sugar group performed better compared to controls during sugar-based reversal learning. In humans under controlled exposure, cue-potentiated motivation increased without a change in explicit valuation, consistent with a signature prediction of incentive sensitization.

items.title: Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy vs Surgery for Stage IA Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is a well-established alternative to surgery for nonoperable patients with early-stage non-small cell (NSCLC) lung cancer. However, the role of SBRT in operable patients is unclear as 3 randomized clinical trials comparing SBRT with surgery were closed early because of poor accrual. Existing observational comparisons are limited by confounding because patients who receive SBRT are generally frailer and more comorbid.
OBJECTIVE: To compare cancer-specific mortality between surgery and SBRT using proximal causal inference to adjust for unmeasured confounding due to frailty and comorbidity using proxy variables.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study was a national database analysis of the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER)-Medicare dataset. Three treatment effect estimates were obtained with increasing control of confounding: unadjusted, standard-regression adjusted for measured confounders as in existing studies, and proximally adjusted for unmeasured confounders. Participants were patients with stage IA NSCLC who underwent sublobar resection or SBRT from 2010 to 2019, followed up through December 21, 2021. Data analysis was performed from April 2023 to August 2026.
EXPOSURES: Sublobar resection vs SBRT. Negative control exposures were constructed from billing codes.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: Lung cancer-specific mortality. Negative control outcomes were constructed from other-cause mortality. Results are reported as hazard differences (HD) and 95% CI.
RESULTS: A total of 4251 patients met inclusion and exclusion criteria; 2581 (60.7%) were female and 1670 (39.3%) were male. Their mean (SD) age was 75.6 (6.3) years. A total of 2558 patients underwent SBRT and 1693 underwent surgery. In the unadjusted and covariate-adjusted analyses, SBRT was associated with higher lung cancer cause-specific mortality, HD of 0.047 person-years (95% CI, 0.038-0.055) and 0.024 person-years (95% CI, 0.014-0.034), respectively. However, there was also compelling evidence of confounding due to a strong estimated association with other-cause mortality. In the proximal analysis, other-cause mortality together with negative control exposures were used to indirectly control for hidden confounders, yielding an HD of 0.012 person-years (95% CI, 0.0013-0.027).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study empirically showed that existing observational comparisons of SBRT and surgery are biased because of unmeasured confounding. When proximal causal inference was used to better control for confounding due to frailty and comorbidity, there continued to be a smaller but significant improvement in outcomes associated with surgery, though the effects of residual bias due to differences in pathologic and clinical staging could not be ruled out. This study demonstrates that proximal causal inference can be used to control for unmeasured confounders in a variety of settings.

items.title: Digital Delivery of Apolipoprotein E Genotype and Phosphorylated Tau 217 Results: The eSMARTER Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Patients are increasingly learning Alzheimer disease (AD) genetic and biomarker results through electronic health portals. Evaluation of alternative scalable delivery models for return of AD risk information is needed to best support patient knowledge and psychological well-being.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a digital platform is comparable to clinician-mediated telehealth sessions for returning apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype and plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) results on outcomes of knowledge and psychological well-being.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The Evaluation of Self-Mediated Alternatives for Risk Testing Education and Return of Results (eSMARTER) study was a noninferiority trial of a digital platform compared to clinician-mediated return of APOE genotype and optional p-tau217 results. Enrollment was conducted October 2024 through February 2025. Follow-up was completed November 2025. This was a decentralized, fully remote trial taking place across the contiguous US. Eligible participants were aged 60 to 80 years and had previously undergone APOE genotyping (without disclosure) via GeneMatch, passed psychological screening, had internet access, and could speak English. Of the 13 033 people invited by GeneMatch, 2052 accepted, and 813 were assessed for eligibility. Of 666 randomized, 651 were ultimately included.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized, 2:1, to the eSMARTER digital platform or study clinician-mediated return of APOE genotype. Following the 6-month post-APOE assessment, participants were offered optional p-tau217 disclosure via the same randomized modality.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes at 1 to 7 days following APOE disclosure included changes in anxiety, disease-specific distress, and AD-related knowledge within a priori noninferiority margins.
RESULTS: A total of 674 persons were eligible and provided demographic information. Of these, 651 participants had been randomized to study clinician-mediated (n = 216) or digital disclosure (n = 435) and completed APOE disclosure (mean [SD] age, 68 [4.7] years; 439 [67%] female; mean [SD] telephone Montreal Cognitive Assessment score, 19 [2]; 66 [10%] APOE4 homozygotes, 377 [58%] heterozygotes, and 208 [32%] noncarriers) A total of 604 participants completed the study; 500 completed optional p-tau217 disclosure. Baseline characteristics were balanced across groups. At 1 to 7 days following APOE disclosure, scores on AD-related knowledge, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Anxiety T-score, and disease-specific distress measures met noninferiority.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Return of APOE genotype by the eSMARTER digital platform is noninferior to study clinician-mediated telehealth disclosure. No significant between-group differences were found following return of p-tau217 results. Together, these results suggest that this digital platform may provide an evidence-based scalable approach for returning AD genetic and biomarker results.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06459583.

items.title: Physical activity coaching and text messaging for adults with mobility limitations (ComeBACK): hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of a physical activity coaching intervention compared with text messaging intervention and waitlist control in adults with mobility limitations.
DESIGN: Three arm, pragmatic, superiority, hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial.
SETTING: Health services and general communities across five Australian states, 19 December 2018 to 7 March 2023.
PARTICIPANTS: 512 community dwelling adults (≥18 years) who self-reported mobility limitations (difficulty or inability to walk 800 m, with or without a walking aid) but were still able to leave home without physical assistance from another person.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 allocation ratio to: a six month, multicomponent intervention including fortnightly physiotherapist delivered telephone coaching (coaching group, n=172); a six month, multicomponent intervention including regular unidirectional text messages (texting group, n=171); and no intervention for six months, followed by the six month text messaging intervention (waitlist control group, n=169). Participants and physiotherapists were unmasked to group allocation.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was device measured mean daily steps at six months, analysed according to treatment allocation using all available data. Outcome assessors and data analysts were masked to group allocation.
RESULTS: Participants' mean age was 69 years (standard deviation (SD) 10 years) and 76% (n=388/511) were women. More than half (n=263/508, 51%) of participants reported multiple long term conditions as the main reason for their mobility limitation. At six months, mean daily steps were 931 higher (95% confidence interval 409 to 1452 steps; P=0.001) in the coaching group (mean 7256 (SD 3736) steps) compared with waitlist group (6526 (3003) steps); and 571 steps higher (58 to 1084, P=0.03) compared with the texting group (6529 (3029) steps). Mean daily steps in the texting group were 359 higher (-91 to 810, P=0.12) compared with the waitlist group, but this was not statistically significant. The number of adverse events was similar between groups (11/172 (6%) in the coaching group, 7/171 (4%) in the texting group, and 13/169 (8%) in the waitlist group) and none were serious.
CONCLUSION: A person centred coaching intervention produced modest increases in physical activity and was more effective than a less intensive texting intervention or no intervention among adults with mobility limitations.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12618001983291.

items.title: Prospective comparison of 28 vs 14 days of venetoclax induction with azacitidine in older adults with untreated AML: OPTI-AML trial.
items.abstract: Azacitidine (Aza) plus venetoclax (Ven) is standard treatment for older/unfit patients with newly diagnosed (ND) acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The approved 28-day Ven schedule is associated with prolonged cytopenias and frequent treatment modifications. Retrospective studies show similar efficacy and reduced toxicity with abbreviated Ven dosing, but prospective data are lacking. OPTI-AML is a prospective randomized phase 2 trial comparing 28-day Ven (AV28) vs 14-day (AV14) with Aza (75 mg/m2 for 7 days) for cycles 1-2 in genomically agnostic patients with ND-AML aged ≥60 years. The primary end point was complete remission (CR) rate within 2 cycles. Between 2023 and 2025, 169 patients received AV28 (n = 83) or AV14 (n = 86). CR rate was 49.4% (AV28) vs 43% (AV14); difference of 6.4% (90% confidence interval: -6.1% to 19.0%), not meeting noninferiority criteria. Patients with NPM1/ IDH2 mutations had higher CR rates with AV28 (60.9% vs 33.3%), whereas rates were equivalent (45%) for other subgroups. Composite CR rates were 80.7% (AV28) vs 68.6% (AV14), and measurable residual disease negativity was similar (77.6% vs 76.5%). Although AV28 had more frequent treatment interruptions, count recovery after cycle 2, grade ≥3 adverse events, and early mortality were similar. In conclusion, AV14 did not demonstrate noninferiority compared with AV28 during cycles 1-2 in an unselected ND-AML cohort. Although the difference in CR rates was not significantly different between arms, these findings do not support routine abbreviation of Ven to 14 days during initial therapy. Certain subgroups may benefit from prolonged Ven exposure, warranting validation in larger studies, especially as triplet regimens evolve. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT03013998.

items.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in surgically resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (PRIME-HCC): a prospective, phase 1b, single-arm trial and translational analyses.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated this combination as neoadjuvant therapy and investigated its effect on peripheral immunity and the tumour microenvironment.
METHODS: PRIME-HCC is a single-arm, phase 1b trial in adults (aged ≥18 years) with early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, Child-Pugh A liver function, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1. Patients received nivolumab (3 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 22 of the first and second cycle) and ipilimumab (1 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of the first cycle only) before liver resection. The primary endpoint was safety, assessed by treatment-related delays to surgery and adverse events in the intention-to-treat population. Translational analyses included imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on paired tumour samples, peripheral immunophenotyping, T-cell receptor (TCR) β sequencing, and longitudinal tumour-agnostic circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) profiling. This trial was registered with EudraCT (2018-000987-27) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03682276); follow-up is currently ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between Sept 18, 2019, and Sept 28, 2023, of 43 patients assessed for eligibility, 33 patients were enrolled (25 [76%] male and 8 [24%] female; median age 68 years [range 38-80; IQR 63-73]); median follow-up was 25·7 months (95% CI 21·2-30·1). Any-grade adverse events occurred in 31 (94%) of patients, with treatment-related adverse events (trAEs) in 25 (76%) patients. Grade 3 trAEs occurred in three (9%) patients (transaminase elevation, anaemia, and dyspnoea). Serious adverse events were recorded in three (9%) patients, and no grade 4-5 events or treatment-related deaths occurred. 30 (91%) patients underwent surgery, including two (6%) who had immune checkpoint inhibitor-related surgical delays. Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 was noted in eight (25%; 95% CI 13-42) patients (one complete response and seven partial responses), with 31 (97%; 84-100) patients achieving disease control. The absence of ctDNA after surgery was associated with improved 2-year recurrence-free survival (nine [82%] of 11 patients vs two [29%] of seven; p=0·049), as was at least 50% ctDNA reduction (median not reached [95% CI not reached] vs 20·9 months [95% CI 16·3-25·4]; HR 0·14 [95% CI 0·02-0·91]; p=0·039). Patients with objective responses showed expansion of peripheral PD-1-positive, Ki-67-positive, CD8-positive T cells (T-responding exhausted cells [Tresp]), associated with higher baseline intratumoral progenitor-exhausted T cells (Tpex) and increased Tresp infiltration. Patients whose disease did not respond to treatment exhibited enrichment of terminally exhausted CD8-positive T cells (Tex-term; CD8-positive PD-1-positive TOX-positive cells) and regulatory T cells.
INTERPRETATION: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab is feasible in early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and later-phase randomised trials are needed to confirm the efficacy of this treatment strategy. Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring could support detection of minimal residual disease and warrants further prospective validation.
FUNDING: Bristol Myers Squibb, Cancer Research UK, Associazione Italiana per la Ricerca sul Cancro, and Foundation for Liver Research.

items.title: Acupoint Thread Embedding for Weight Loss in Women With Overweight or Obesity : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether acupoint thread embedding (ATE), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention, produces weight reduction remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of ATE for weight reduction in women with overweight or obesity.
DESIGN: Randomized, sham-controlled trial masked to participants, outcome assessors, and analysts. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06316310).
SETTING: Acupuncture Department, Shanghai Municipal Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.
PARTICIPANTS: 132 women aged 18 to 45 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 24.0 kg/m2 or greater.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to ATE (6 sessions over 12 weeks) or sham ATE (superficial needle insertion at the same acupoints without manipulation, de qi, thread placement, or needle retention), followed by a 12-week follow-up.
MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was change in BMI from baseline to week 12, analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: At week 12, BMI and body weight decreased 0.7 kg/m2 (95% CI, -1.0 to -0.3 kg/m2) and 1.8 kg (CI, -2.7 to -0.9 kg), respectively, more with ATE than with sham ATE; at week 24, differences were -1.1 kg/m2 (CI, -1.7 to -0.6 kg/m2) and -3.0 kg (CI, -4.5 to -1.6 kg), respectively. Weight reduction of 5% or more occurred in 25.8% versus 9.1% (risk difference, 16.7 percentage points [CI, 3.7 to 29.3 percentage points]) at 12 weeks. Acupoint thread embedding produced greater reductions in waist and hip circumference, body fat percentage, and appetite scores, whereas cardiometabolic and patient-reported outcomes did not differ. Adverse events were mild and comparably distributed.
LIMITATION: Single center, generally healthy women of reproductive age, unmasked acupuncturists, short-term follow-up, and underpowered for uncommon adverse events and subgroup analyses.
CONCLUSION: Acupoint thread embedding produced modest but sustained reductions in BMI and adiposity-related measures in Chinese women of reproductive age with overweight or obesity.
PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Facility for Translational Medicine (Shanghai).

items.title: Eltrombopag plus cyclosporine for moderate aplastic anemia: a placebo-controlled, double-blind phase 3 trial.
items.abstract: Eltrombopag combined with horse antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine (CSA) is the standard of care for patients with severe aplastic anemia who are not eligible for stem cell transplantation. No consensus exists on the optimal treatment of moderate aplastic anemia (MAA). The Eltrombopag for MAA trial is an investigator-initiated, prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, multicenter phase 3 trial that compared eltrombopag plus CSA (n = 41) with placebo plus CSA (n = 44) as a first-line therapy for patients with MAA with clinically significant cytopenia. In patients with evaluable response at week 24 (n = 75), the overall response rate (ORR), including partial response and complete response (CR), was significantly higher in the eltrombopag plus CSA arm (71.4%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 54.8-83.8) than in the placebo plus CSA arm (42.5%; 95% CI, 28.5-57.8; P = .011, Fisher exact test; primary end point). After response assessment at week 24 and unblinding, patients in the placebo arm without CR were switched to receive eltrombopag in addition to continued CSA. items.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass.
items.abstract: Bogong moths (Agrotis infusa) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps1,2. These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds3, suggesting that their magnetic sense4 probably harnesses the Earth's magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet-blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense5.
